sync.prompt: Choose which HubSpot objects to sync

record.label: Records
record.note: relist_diff, because GET /crm/v3/objects/{type} takes no modified-since filter; the search endpoint does, but it is a different node with a different contract. The stored text is the record's properties as sorted JSON, which is what a CRM record honestly is - a name and a body cannot be built out of it with the four operators. NOT LIVE-TESTED: no HubSpot connection exists in dev.

scope_notes: crm.schemas.custom.read is what GET /crm/v3/schemas needs, and hubspot-list_object_types-1 is the only node that calls it. Without it the picker could offer the four standard object types and never a portal's custom ones.
rate_limit_notes: HubSpot publishes its ceiling as a 10-second window, not a minute: a marketplace OAuth app gets 110 requests per 10 seconds per installed account, and an older app gets 100.
rpm 600 is the same thing in the framework's units: a sustained 100 per 10 seconds, the conservative floor rather than the 110 ceiling.
burst 100 is exactly one window's worth fired back to back.
concurrency 5 is our own choice, not HubSpot's. It keeps one batching node from spending a whole window in a single breath while other work shares the connection.
Daily limits (650k on Professional, 1M on Enterprise) sit far above anything one workspace spends, so they are not modeled. A 429 pauses the bucket either way.
